name: Any.do
subcategory: personal tasks, routines and daily planning
tagline: Manage personal tasks, lists, reminders, recurring items, and a daily planning flow

pricing.notes: Typical Premium monthly rate; annual billing is lower.

tiers.name: Personal
tiers.limits: 1.5 MB attachment limit; 1 priority tag; 5 Any.do Moment sessions/month; no numeric task/list cap published.

tiers.name: Premium
tiers.limits: Unlimited recurring tasks, reminders, color tags, and Moment sessions; larger attachments.

tiers.name: Family
tiers.limits: Up to 4 family members; up to 4 shared family boards.

tiers.name: Workspace
tiers.limits: 1 to unlimited members; unlimited boards; 100+ workflow templates.

pricing.freeTierCaps: 1.5 MB attachment limit; 1 priority tag; 5 Any.do Moment sessions/month; no numeric task/list cap published.
pricing.billingTerms: monthly + annual; Family is flat for up to 4 members; Workspace is per member
pricing.hiddenCosts: Workspace bills each member; Family is capped at 4 members and 4 shared boards.

verdictSummary: The core loop is small enough for a capable coding agent to produce a useful local version in one sitting. For Any.do, manage personal tasks, lists, reminders, recurring items, and a daily planning flow. The hard boundary is mobile capture, widgets, family features, calendar integration, and sync, plus cross-device reliability and workflow polish.
coreLoopDIY: Capture tasks, lists, and reminders, schedule or repeat them, work from a focused daily planning view, and keep history locally.
whatYouLose: mobile capture, widgets, family features, calendar integration, and sync
ongoingBurden: recurrence edge cases, notifications, sync conflicts, calendar APIs, mobile capture, and backups
whyPeopleStillPay: People still pay for Any.do because task software is sticky because trust, speed, and ubiquitous capture matter more than the database schema. The recurring cost buys recurrence edge cases, notifications, sync conflicts, calendar APIs, mobile capture, and backups, not just the visible interface.

priorArt.name: Vikunja
priorArt.desc: Mature open-source task and project manager with lists, kanban, and recurring work.

alternatives.name: Microsoft To Do
alternatives.desc: A polished free task manager, paid for with a Microsoft account rather than money

facts.install: Install the Windows, macOS, iOS, or Android app, or use the web app, and sign in with a Microsoft account
facts.dataFormat: Tasks are stored as structured records on Microsoft's Exchange Online servers and surface in Outlook Tasks across synchronized clients
facts.gapVsPaid: Microsoft To Do does not combine tasks and calendar in Any.do’s broad cross-platform daily-planning flow or reproduce its family and smart-grocery features.

alternatives.name: Vikunja
alternatives.desc: A capable Todoist replacement once you accept becoming its hosting department

facts.install: Use the paid hosted service or deploy the free server with Docker Compose, a package, or the standalone binary
facts.dataFormat: Tasks, projects, users, and settings live in SQLite, MySQL/MariaDB, or PostgreSQL, with attachments in a persistent files directory, on the selected host
facts.gapVsPaid: Vikunja lacks Any.do’s polished guided daily planner, consumer-grade reminders, calendar experience, and low-friction mobile setup.
facts.setupBlocker: The free path requires a server or Docker, persistent volumes, secrets, and normally a reverse proxy with TLS

alternatives.name: Apple Reminders
alternatives.desc: Things minus the polish tax, provided every device in sight has an Apple logo

facts.install: Preinstalled on iPhone, iPad, and Mac; enable iCloud or another supported reminders account for synchronization
facts.engines: Optional Apple Intelligence can suggest or auto-categorize reminders on supported devices; ordinary task management does not require AI
facts.dataFormat: Structured reminder records live in iCloud or another configured reminders account and are cached on Apple devices; iCloud provides account-level restore rather than user-visible task files
facts.gapVsPaid: Apple Reminders lacks Any.do’s guided My Day flow and broad Windows, Android, and web support.

alternatives.name: Tasks.org
alternatives.desc: A serious Android task list with recurrence and reminders; desktop and CalDAV sync are paid

facts.install: Install the Android app from Google Play or F-Droid; an early desktop app is optional
facts.dataFormat: Tasks are local and offline-first on Android; optional synchronization targets Google Tasks, Microsoft To Do, Tasks.org Cloud, CalDAV/DAVx5, EteSync, or DecSync
facts.gapVsPaid: Tasks.org is Android-first, with no mature iOS or web client and a much less polished calendar and daily-planning experience than Any.do.
facts.setupBlocker: Local Android use is straightforward, but most non-Google/Microsoft synchronization options require an in-app subscription or separately configured sync service, and desktop support is still early

notes: Editorial comparison targets the Premium plan and a personal desktop task manager DIY substitute. Recheck price before merge.
prompt:
Build a personal replacement for Any.do in an empty repository.
Use Tauri 2, React, TypeScript, SQLite, and desktop notifications; do not offer alternative stacks.
The core loop is: capture tasks, lists, and reminders, schedule or repeat them, work from a focused daily planning view, and keep history locally.
Make the first run work locally with one documented command.
Store all user data locally by default and make export straightforward.
Put secrets in .env, ship .env.example, and never commit credentials.
Create inbox, today, upcoming, someday, and completed views with fast keyboard capture.
Support projects, tags, due dates, start dates, priorities, notes, subtasks, and attachments.
Implement robust daily, weekly, monthly, and custom recurring rules with tests.
Add a focus view with one active task, timer, and optional desktop notification.
Provide search, saved filters, undo, and a completed-task archive.
Export and import a documented JSON format and make automatic local backups.
Include clear empty, loading, success, and recoverable error states.
Add input validation, safe filenames, and graceful handling of unavailable APIs.
Write focused tests for the core transformation and one end-to-end happy path.
Create a README with setup, architecture, permissions, data location, and backup steps.
Do not add accounts, billing, telemetry, analytics, or a hosted control plane.
Deliberately leave out team assignment and comments.
Deliberately leave out two-way calendar or email synchronization.
Deliberately leave out native mobile apps and cloud accounts.
Finish by running the tests and listing the exact commands used.
